label: Search Admin (Server RBAC role)
type: a Server RBAC role, one of the 56 in learn/security/roles.md. NOT a privilege: Server's concrete role catalogue has no separately enumerable privilege tier. Do NOT confuse with the privilege:capella-advanced-access-fts-* family, which is Capella's genuinely separate privilege catalogue and has its own distinct ids for Search access.
note: Re-filed from privilege: to role: in round 12, in the same sweep as the nine query_* ids. roles.md documents this as one of 56 Server RBAC roles, with its own 'Role: <label> (<internal_name>)' table and prose calling it a role outright. Two ids for one role, now folded: privilege:fts-admin (1 file, fts-introduction.md, the internal-name form) and privilege:search-admin (3 files, the three create-search-index pages, the label form). Neither was promoted, so the split was invisible to the promotion rule - each sat below the recurrence bar alone while the role they both name clears it at 4. That is the id-normalization problem costing a real promotion, not just tidiness.
